claims: Artemis II successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Artemis II lifted off on a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II is a 10-day mission to orbit the Moon.
Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion capsule.
Artemis II is designed to test systems and orbit the Moon.
The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II launch had minor, expected technical issues.
The Artemis II launch had a temporary sensor issue.
The temporary sensor issue did not affect the Artemis II mission.
After launching, the Orion spacecraft is scheduled to separate from the upper stage of the rocket.
After launching, the Orion spacecraft is scheduled to proceed with its lunar journey.
Artemis II is part of NASA's program to return humans to the Moon and pave the way for future lunar landings.
